payload.claim: Acceptance criterion 2 requires that 'a reverted run that errored, or that did not enumerate, is still a `skip` whatever it reports' — explicitly covering the case where an errored/non-enumerated run also happens to report `uncollected`. No test exercises that combination: every skip-path test (`test_a_reverted_run_that_could_not_produce_a_result_is_a_skip_not_an_error`, `test_a_reverted_run_that_did_not_enumerate_is_a_skip`, and the inline `unreadable` case in `test_a_handed_name_the_reverted_run_does_not_account_for_is_an_error`) leaves `uncollected` at its default `None`. Changing the status check at this line to `if reverted_result.status not in ("pass", "fail") and reverted_result.uncollected is None:` would let a malformed run that reports `status="error"` alongside a populated `uncollected` fall through into the new accounting logic instead of returning `skip` as the criterion requires — and every existing test, none of which sets `uncollected` on an error/non-enumeration run, would stay green.
